title: ingress-friction-slowpath-probe-scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory runs to characterize "slowpath" friction at ingress — i.e., the latency penalty introduced when a request hits code paths that bypass fast-path batching/cache (KV miss, model-switch, demultiplexing to cold worker, or cold-queue insertion). Goal is to gather reproducible microbenchmarks, note triggers, and sketch mitigations to test in a follow-up runbook.

Background/context:
- Observed customer reports of token-p99 spikes during short surges (~5–30s) even when overall QPS is low. Suspect ingress-level phenomena (queue insert ordering, early demux to colder worker, missing prefix cache hits) rather than GPU cold-start.
- Related tickets: CON-2387 (customer incident), ENG-542 (early demux gating change).

Quick hypothesis list (ranked):
1) KV cache miss + synchronous fetch from store (cold path) adds ~10–40ms per request head + extra queuing jitter.
2) Burst demux heuristic: first few requests after idle are routed to lower-util workers (warmup penalty) causing serializing delays.
3) Slowpath processing (tracing, auth check fallback) enters when certain header patterns present -> extra 5–15ms.
4) Batching timeout increases on low concurrency leading to higher tail for small bursts.

Environment and config used for probes:
- Cluster: dev-fleet-3 (mixed A100/V100 pool, 4 GPU nodes)
- Runtime branch: probe/ingress-slowpath-2025 (see PR #789)
- Runtime flags: --kv-cache=enabled --kv-inline-ttl=30s --demux-policy=fast-bias-off --batching.window-ms=8
- Client driver: synthetic-arrival v0.9 (Poisson + 3x microbursts generator)
- Workload: small-gen (avg prompt 64 tokens, generate 32 tokens), open-model-replica quantized 8-bit

Commands (local harness):
- run: ./bench/ingress_probe --profile=microburst --burst=20x2s --base-qps=8 --duration=600 --out=run-2026-03-10.log
- sampling: jq -r '.samples|map(.p99)[]' run-2026-03-10.log | awk '{print NR, $1}\n'

Representative raw observations (selected excerpts):
- baseline steady: base qps 8, p50=12ms, p95=26ms, p99=42ms
- single microburst (20 reqs over 2s): immediate p99 spike to 180–230ms for first 2s, then recovers to baseline in ~6s
- correlation: ~78% of spiky p99 traces coincide with a KV-store GET latency spike (from metrics) that lasts 50–150ms (likely due to cache eviction/refresh)

Small table (aggregated moments) from run-2026-03-10.log:
- window "pre-burst": requests=4800, p50=11ms, p95=25ms, p99=41ms
- window "burst-0..2s": requests=1200, p50=15ms, p95=75ms, p99=201ms
- window "recovery 2..10s": requests=2400, p50=13ms, p95=29ms, p99=58ms

Trace anecdote (one slow request):
- trace id: 20260310-09:14:12-abc123
- path: ingress -> auth fast (miss) -> demux to worker-7 (cold slot) -> kv-cache miss -> sync-store-get(128ms) -> enqueue local small-batch -> cpu scheduling wait (12ms) -> start token gen
- sum(ms): demux 8 + kv-get 128 + enqueue wait 12 + scheduling 12 + model overhead 20 = ~180ms

Quick experiments run (notes):
A) Turn off inline KV fetch (let callers do best-effort): p99 drops to 110–130ms during bursts but recovery slower (longer tail window).
B) Increase batching.window-ms to 12ms: p95 improves slightly during bursts (from 75->62ms) but p50 increases ~2ms (expected).
C) Enable demux fast-bias: more requests routed to hot workers; p99 for bursts drops to 95–120ms but observed higher contention at steady QPS=8 in some runs -> OOM risk on small nodes.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why KV-store sees 50–150ms spikes: is it external (redis persistence, GC) or local evictions + miss amplification? Need to correlate with infra logs (redis AOF rewrite schedule?)
- Are we double-penalizing requests that miss cache and also hit a cold demux? (i.e., two sequential slow decisions)
- How much of the p99 is queuing vs pure processing? Need to instrument per-segment queue length histograms at 10ms resolution.

Next experiments (prioritized):
1) Run with KV-store metrics at 1s granularity and enable redis CLIENT LIST sampling during bursts. (owner: Ravi)
2) Test prefetching/pinned prefix warmup: when client has prefix X, preemptively touch cache for next expected tokens. Short-run: simulate with synthetic prefix set and measure p99 delta. (owner: Lydia)
3) Implement lightweight async-kv-get fallback: return partial response while kv fetch continues; measure correctness tradeoffs. (owner: Marta)

Practical mitigations to prototype quickly:
- Safe demux bias: keep fast-bias ON for first 4 requests of an observed connection, fallback to normal policy after. This reduces first-request slow hits without global hotspots.
- Soft-prefetch: on detecting a short burst, issue async kv-touch for expected prefixes for next 2s window.
- Tail-aware batching: when ingress sees sudden burst, temporarily reduce batching.window-ms for new arrivals to force smaller but faster batches.

Quick to-dos (actionable):
- [ ] Add per-segment queue length histograms to tracing (10ms bins). (Marta)
- [ ] Correlate redis AOF/compact ops with observed KV spikes (infra). (Ravi)
- [ ] Schedule a 1-hour focused run with pinned prefetch scenario next Tuesday. (Lydia)

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- The slowpath is noisy and multi-factor. We should avoid a single "fix" and instead create a short runbook of layered defenses.
- Keep experiments small and reproducible; stash a deterministic generator for burst shapes used in all follow-ups.
- Consider adding a synthetic "warm primer" traffic that runs at extremely low QPS but touches hot prefixes to reduce first-hit penalties for important customers.
